e-12702.problem:
Consider the following statement.

$P: 1$ is **not** smaller than $2$

What statement represents $\neg P?$
e-12702.worked_solution:
The symbol "$\neg$" represents negation. So, our task is to negate the given sentence. 

To negate our plain English sentence, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

It is **not** true that $1$ is **not** smaller than $2.$

In other words, $1$ is smaller than $2.$ Therefore, $\neg P$ means the following:

$1$ is smaller than $2.$

Note that $P$ is **false,** while $\neg P$ is **true.**

e-12681.problem:
Consider the following statement:

$\dfrac12$ is **not** a natural number, or $\sqrt{2}$ is **not** a real number.

Express the compound statement above in symbolic form given the following:

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095811/assets/5aa4f3afde005cff577fd75ebfa69e37861edf2628383b1191bf5c07b30fdde6.png)

e-12681.worked_solution:
The sentence

 $\dfrac12$ is **not** a natural number 

can be expressed symbolically as $\neg P.$ 

The sentence

$\sqrt{2}$ is **not** a real number 

can be expressed symbolically as $\neg Q.$

Therefore, the sentence

 $\dfrac12$ is **not** a natural number, or $\sqrt{2}$ is **not** a real number

can be expressed symbolically as $\neg P \lor \neg Q.$

e-12682.knowledge_point: Completing a Truth Table for a Compound Statement
e-12682.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\, \neg (P \land \neg Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\phantom{F}}$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\phantom{F}}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\phantom{F}}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\phantom{F}}$ |
e-12682.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for $\neg Q.$ Remember that the truth values of $\neg Q$ are opposite those of $Q.$

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\, \neg Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ |

Then, we add a column for $P \land \neg Q.$ Remember that $P \land \neg Q$ is true if both $P$ and $\neg Q$ are true.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\, \neg Q\,$ | $\, P \land \neg Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ |

Finally, we add a column for $\neg ( P \land \neg Q ).$ Remember that the truth values of $\neg (P \land \neg Q)$ are opposite those of $P \land \neg Q.$

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\, \neg Q\,$ | $\, P \land \neg Q\,$ | $\, \neg (P \land \neg Q) \,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |

e-12683.worked_solution:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So: 

- we can simplify $\neg(\neg C)$ to $C,$ and

- we can also simplify $\neg(\neg(C \land D))$ to $C \land D.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to 

$$
C \lor (C \land D).
$$

after.problem:

$$
P:0\text{ is }\text{not}\text{ greater than }0.1
$$

 
which of the following represents $¬P?$
after.worked_solution:
The symbol "$¬$" represents negation. So, our task is to negate the given sentence. 

To negate our plain English sentence, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

$$
¬P:\text{It is }\text{not}\text{ true that }0\text{ is }\text{not}\text{ greater than }0.1,
$$

$$
¬P:0\text{ is greater than }0.1.
$$

Note that $P$ is **true,** while $¬P$ is **false.**

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
